concepts.name: Constitutional Basis and Establishment of Finance Commission
key_dimensions: Article 280: Mandatory vs discretionary nature of FC constitution
President's power to constitute FC vs Parliament's role in defining qualifications
Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951 — statutory framework
Quasi-judicial character of FC and its non-permanent nature

concepts.name: Composition and Qualification of Finance Commission Members
key_dimensions: Chairman's qualification: experience in public affairs (not necessarily economics)
Four other members: qualifications specified by Parliament via legislation, not Constitution
Part-time vs full-time members — constitutional silence and legislative discretion
Reappointment eligibility and conditions of service

concepts.name: Terms of Reference (ToR) of the Finance Commission
key_dimensions: Mandatory ToR under Article 280(3): tax devolution, grants-in-aid, consolidated fund of states
Additional ToR by President — scope and limits (e.g., local body grants, disaster relief)
Evolution of ToR across successive FCs — expanding mandate beyond fiscal transfers
Distinction between what FC must address vs what it may address

concepts.name: Vertical Devolution: Division of Taxes Between Union and States
key_dimensions: Divisible pool composition — taxes included and excluded (cess, surcharges excluded)
Progressive increase in states' share: 11th FC (29.5%) to 14th FC (42%) to 15th FC (41%)
Rationale for reduction from 42% to 41% in 15th FC (J&K reorganization)
UPSC trap: cess and surcharges not part of divisible pool — fiscal centralization concern

concepts.name: Horizontal Devolution: Criteria for Distribution Among States
key_dimensions: Criteria used: population, area, income distance, forest cover, demographic performance, tax effort
Shift from 1971 census (used by 1st–13th FC) to 2011 census by 15th FC — political controversy
Demographic performance criterion: reward for population control (replaces population criterion partially)
Tension between equity (poorer states) and efficiency (better-performing states) in criteria design

concepts.name: Grants-in-Aid under Article 275
key_dimensions: Article 275: Grants to states in need of assistance — not all states, only needy ones
Distinction between grants under Article 275 (FC mandate) vs Article 282 (discretionary grants by Union/States)
Post-devolution revenue deficit grants — compensatory nature
Sector-specific grants: local bodies, disaster management, health, education — 15th FC innovation

concepts.name: Finance Commission vs Planning Commission / NITI Aayog
key_dimensions: FC: constitutional body; Planning Commission/NITI Aayog: executive/advisory body
Historical overlap: Plan vs Non-Plan expenditure — FC covered non-plan, PC covered plan (now merged)
Abolition of Plan/Non-Plan distinction and its impact on FC's role post-2017
NITI Aayog has no fund transfer role; FC retains constitutional mandate for transfers

concepts.name: Consolidated Fund of India and States — FC's Role
key_dimensions: FC recommendations relate to Consolidated Fund of India, not Contingency Fund or Public Account
Charged vs voted expenditure: FC recommendations are binding in spirit but require parliamentary approval
Article 266 vs Article 267 — relevance to FC transfers
States' Consolidated Fund augmentation as FC's constitutional purpose

concepts.name: Finance Commission and Local Bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities)
key_dimensions: Article 280(3)(bb) and (c) added by 73rd/74th Amendment — FC must recommend grants for local bodies
State Finance Commissions (SFCs) vs Central Finance Commission — two-tier structure, frequent confusion
15th FC: first to give separate grants for urban and rural local bodies with tied/untied distinction
Performance-based grants for local bodies — conditionalities attached

concepts.name: State Finance Commissions (SFCs) — Relationship with Central FC
key_dimensions: Constitutional mandate under Articles 243-I (Panchayats) and 243-Y (Municipalities)
SFCs constituted by State governments — not by President; Governor-appointed
Central FC uses SFC reports as inputs — but SFC recommendations are for intra-state distribution
Criticism: SFCs often non-functional or reports not acted upon — democratic deficit at sub-state level

concepts.name: 15th Finance Commission — Key Recommendations and Innovations
key_dimensions: Two reports: interim (2020-21) and final (2021-26) — unique feature due to COVID-19
Retention of 41% vertical share; introduction of 'performance-based' incentive grants
Defense and internal security funding — first time FC addressed this (non-lapsable fund)
Sector-specific tied grants for health, education, agriculture — departure from earlier untied approach

concepts.name: Fiscal Federalism and Finance Commission's Role in Centre-State Relations
key_dimensions: FC as primary institutional mechanism for fiscal equalization in Indian federalism
Asymmetric fiscal federalism: states have expenditure responsibilities exceeding revenue powers
Criticism of growing cess/surcharge revenue bypassing divisible pool — centralizing tendency
FC recommendations and their impact on fiscal autonomy vs fiscal dependence of states

concepts.name: Disaster Management Grants and Finance Commission
key_dimensions: State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF) — FC recommends corpus
FC's role post-Disaster Management Act, 2005 — overlap and coordination
15th FC: recommended separate grants for disaster management with focus on mitigation
UPSC trap: NDRF is not managed by FC — it is under MHA; FC only recommends funding levels

concepts.name: Revenue Deficit Grants under Finance Commission
key_dimensions: Post-devolution revenue deficit: when state's revenue expenditure exceeds revenue receipts after FC devolution
Tapering grants: designed to incentivize states to reduce deficits over FC award period
15th FC: 17 states eligible for revenue deficit grants — not all states qualify
Distinction from Article 275 grants — revenue deficit grants are compensatory, not developmental

concepts.name: FC Recommendations: Binding Nature and Implementation
key_dimensions: FC is advisory — recommendations not automatically binding on the President/Parliament
Convention vs compulsion: government has generally accepted FC tax devolution recommendations
Selective acceptance: Union can accept some and reject other recommendations (especially grants)
Action Taken Report (ATR): government must lay ATR before Parliament — accountability mechanism

concepts.name: Tax Devolution Mechanism: Monthly Releases and Back-to-Back Loans
key_dimensions: Monthly devolution by CGA based on FC-recommended shares — automatic transfer mechanism
COVID-19 period: back-to-back loans to states in lieu of GST compensation — not FC mechanism
Difference between FC-mandated transfers and Finance Ministry's discretionary releases
UPSC trap: GST Compensation to states is NOT an FC function — it is under GST (Compensation to States) Act

concepts.name: GST and Its Impact on Finance Commission's Role
key_dimensions: GST subsumed many state taxes — changed nature of divisible pool calculation
GST Council vs Finance Commission — different constitutional bases, different mandates
GST compensation cess excluded from divisible pool — states' concern about shrinking pool
FC's challenge: recommending shares when GST revenue is uncertain and buoyancy is variable

concepts.name: Successive Finance Commissions — Evolution of Philosophy
key_dimensions: 1st FC (K.C. Neogy, 1952): established baseline; minimal grants, limited devolution
10th FC: introduced principle-based formula replacing ad hoc approach
14th FC (Y.V. Reddy): historic jump to 42% — 'Big Bang' devolution, reduced centrally sponsored schemes
15th FC (N.K. Singh): performance incentives, tied grants, defense funding — new paradigm

concepts.name: Finance Commission and Fiscal Consolidation / FRBM
key_dimensions: FC mandated to review states' fiscal capacity — links to FRBM compliance
FC may recommend conditionalities tied to fiscal discipline for grants
15th FC recommended fiscal consolidation roadmap for both Centre and states post-COVID
Tension: FC promoting expenditure devolution vs FRBM promoting deficit reduction

concepts.name: Excluded Items from Divisible Pool — Cess, Surcharges, and Non-Tax Revenue
key_dimensions: Constitutional position: only 'taxes' in Union List (Article 270) form divisible pool — non-tax revenue excluded
Cess and surcharges: constitutionally permissible exclusions — but growing share raises federalism concerns
Share of cess/surcharge in gross tax revenue grew from ~3% to ~15%+ — fiscal centralization
UPSC trap: States have no constitutional claim on cess/surcharge — FC cannot include them in divisible pool
